mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5pp over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this joint trigger occurs (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 3-month moving averages signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 3-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies are above their 3-month MA (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE dynamics) above 0.2 percentage points for four consecutive months, combined with stable payroll employment growth (PAYEMS), signals improved labor supply without wage pressure, which supports corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive under these conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) and S&P 500 returns exists such that monthly increases in RSAFS above 0.5% predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS > 0.5% monthly change and positive S&P 500 5-day returns falls below 0.3 in any 12-month rolling window.
